text: The IAM statement AllowPartnerAccessKey that grants kms:Encrypt/kms:Decrypt must carry the same Null condition on kms:EncryptionContext:salesman_id as the key policy's AllowPartnerAccessWrapBoundToSalesman statement, otherwise partner access is not actually bound to a salesman.
author: bohdantanasov
why: Reviewer caught that AllowPartnerAccessKey had no salesman_id condition while the key policy statement it mirrors did, and commit cfffb8a added the matching condition.
do: When editing either the role's AllowPartnerAccessKey statement or the key policy's AllowPartnerAccessWrapBoundToSalesman statement, keep their kms:EncryptionContext:salesman_id conditions in sync.

text: The service-tokens DynamoDB table ARN in PlatformIntegrationsStack must be built from the table name constant (CommonResourcesStack.ServiceTokensTableName), not from a cross-stack token reference to the CommonResourcesStack construct.
author: bohdantanasov
why: Reviewer noted a cross-stack token reference would make CDK create a generated export in stack-common that both environments' stacks depend on, instead of following the repo's explicit commonStack.ExportValue(...) pattern.
do: When referencing resources from CommonResourcesStack elsewhere, pass the resource name/ARN as a string constant or explicit ExportValue, never a direct cross-stack construct/token reference.

text: The run queue's message retention, the DLQ's retention, the STALE_QUEUED_MS threshold, and the MetricApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage alarm threshold must stay ordered consistently (alarm threshold < STALE_QUEUED_MS < queue retention < DLQ retention) so stale-message detection and the age alarm both have time to fire before messages are dropped.
author: bohdantanasov
why: Reviewer flagged in infrastructure#169 that the run queue's Duration.Hours(1) retention was shorter than the 45-minute STALE_QUEUED_MS while the alarm fires at 20 minutes, and the fix aligned these values across PlatformIntegrationsStack.cs.
do: When touching queue retention, DLQ retention, STALE_QUEUED_MS, or the age-of-oldest-message alarm threshold in PlatformIntegrationsStack.cs, re-check that all four values stay in the correct relative order.

text: Secrets Manager paths for integration clients must stay under a prefix already covered by an IAM policy (e.g. `integrations/*` granted in CommonResourcesStack.cs:519 and :971); the rotation role and deploy policy only have read access to prefixes explicitly referenced there.
author: bohdantanasov
why: Reviewer noted CommonResourcesStack.cs:519 and :971 grant read on `integrations/*`, while the new `partner-access-web` client maps to `partner-access/{env}/…`, a prefix no policy in src references.
do: When adding a new integrations client/secret prefix in PlatformIntegrationsStack.cs, add or extend a matching IAM policy grant in CommonResourcesStack.cs (or reuse the `integrations/*` prefix) so the rotation role and deploy policy can read it.

text: In the platform integrations stack, the KMS key and the credentials table must keep RemovalPolicy.RETAIN, while the runs table and the files bucket are RemovalPolicy.DESTROY by design.
author: bohdantanasov
why: Review on infrastructure#169 confirmed that only the KMS key (PlatformIntegrationsStack.cs:129) and credentials table (:145) are RETAIN, while the runs table (:159) and files bucket (:233) are DESTROY.
do: Before changing removal policies on this stack, check which resources are meant to survive a stack delete/redeploy (key, credentials) versus which are expected to be wiped (runs, files), and update the rollback doc if the set changes.

text: The PassRole statement `PassDefaultLambdaSamRole` in the shared `policy-lambda-sam-deploy` policy adds partner-access role ARNs without an `iam:PassedToService` condition, so any principal with that policy can pass those roles to any service, not just Lambda.
author: bohdantanasov
why: Review remark on infrastructure#169 (PRO-10028) flagged this gap; the follow-up fix only documented the deploy principal as a party that can decrypt (docs/platform-integrations-stack.md:35-43, PlatformIntegrationsStack.cs:81-83) but left the PassRole statement itself unscoped (CommonResourcesStack.cs:895-908, :1499-1507).
do: Add an `iam:PassedToService` condition (or split the partner-access role ARNs into a separate, scoped policy) before granting further roles via `policy-lambda-sam-deploy`.

text: The Platform API resource server exposes a single scope, `{platformApiHost}/salesmen`, and this one scope also covers write operations — there is no separate scope for writes to restrict to.
author: bohdantanasov
why: Review thread on PlatformIntegrationsStack.cs:371 confirmed this is the Platform API resource server's only scope and that it covers writes too.
do: When granting or auditing access for clients like eic-cache against the Platform API, assume `salesmen` is the sole scope and covers both reads and writes rather than looking for a write-specific scope.

text: The KMS key policy used by PlatformIntegrationsStack has no root `kms:*` statement, so any IAM identity statement granting `kms:Encrypt`/`kms:Decrypt`/`DescribeKey` on this key must itself carry the `Null` condition on `kms:EncryptionContext:salesman_id` — the key policy will not scope access for you.
author: bohdantanasov
why: Review remark on infrastructure#169 pointed out the identity statement granted kms:Encrypt/Decrypt/DescribeKey with no condition while the key policy lacks a root kms:* statement.
do: When adding or editing any IAM statement that grants kms actions on this key, always include the salesman_id EncryptionContext condition rather than relying on the key policy to restrict access.

text: The business term «Aktivita 90/360» is the boolean salesmen.activity column (shown Áno/Nie in the BO salesman profile); there is no separate 90-day or 360-day activity number anywhere in platform-salesmen.
author: bohdantanasov
why: In PRO-10348 a request for «Aktivita 90/360» was first misread as missing data with no source; nothing in the backend names the field that way, only the frontend i18n key activity90360.
do: When a ticket asks for «Aktivita 90/360», read Salesman::activity; do not look for or invent a 90/360 metric.
